claims.text: The target alloy is equimolar WTaTiVZr.
Standard melting and casting produce a homogeneous distribution of all five elements in WTaTiVZr.
WTaTiVZr has greater high-temperature plastic strain than commercially pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr has greater high-temperature toughness than commercially pure tungsten.
WTaTiVZr contains a uniform distribution of nanoscale coherent precipitates.
The proposed precipitates are Zr-enriched or compositionally related refractory nanoprecipitates.
Coherent nanoprecipitates occur both within the alloy matrix and along grain boundaries.
Coherent precipitate interfaces facilitate dislocation transmission.
Coherent precipitates relieve local stress concentrations that would otherwise promote premature crack initiation.
The precipitates act as distributed barriers to dislocation pile-up.
Precipitate-mediated dislocation transmission delays crack initiation and increases ductility and toughness.
Under high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will exhibit more evenly distributed dislocation motion than pure tungsten.
Under high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will exhibit delayed crack propagation relative to pure tungsten.
Pure tungsten is expected to deform less and respond more brittly because it lacks the proposed nanoscale features.
Approximately 800 °C is representative of the plasma-facing-component temperature regime relevant to the proposed mechanism.
The proposed mechanism remains valid up to approximately 800 °C at service-representative strain rates.
Extreme irradiation or substantial changes in grain size or precipitate distribution may invalidate the mechanism.
Solute drag and grain-boundary effects may also contribute to plasticity and toughness.

contradictions.description: The initial state asserts a homogeneous distribution of all five elements, whereas the hypothesized mediator requires compositionally enriched precipitates, particularly Zr-enriched precipitates. These descriptions conflict unless 'homogeneous' is explicitly limited to a larger length scale.
